Marissa / Jonas —

We reproduced an analogous failure pattern in staging using the customer's request vectors. Quick findings:
- After rolling the "optimized-batching" change on 2026-03-08 (commit f9c8b2), the KV-cache eviction TTL logic started to misalign with the batching scheduler.
- When heavy, bursty traffic hits the batching window, the server spawns larger micro-batches while simultaneously evicting/mis-indexing KV cache entries. That causes cache thrash, increases per-request CPU and memory jitter, and queues start to back up at the router layer.
- Observable signal: queue length climbs, per-request latency jumps from ~300ms to multiple seconds, then requests hit gateway and model timeouts, producing 504s. Retry storms amplify the queueing. We've also seen 429s from our admission controller when it hits the in-flight request cap.

Root-cause hypothesis: an interaction between the new batching coalescer and a TTL edge-case in KV-cache when batch sizes exceed expected sizes (rare under old heuristics). The regression looks to be introduced in the weekend rollout.

Immediate mitigations proposed (order matters):
1) Disable optimized-batching for the affected model variant (fast rollback flag available) — low risk, immediate effect.
2) Increase gateway and model-side timeouts by 50% to buy headroom while we patch.
3) Apply backpressure at the ingress (short-term rate-limiting per-customer) for Acme only while mitigation rolls out.
4) Hotfix INF-4721 to fix TTL alignment and add unit tests; target: hotfix branch with canary in 2 hours, full rollout in 6 hours pending validation.

I'll open INF-4721 now and attach the reproducer. Need ops to coordinate the rollback + ingress rule, and CS to confirm the timeline with the customer.

Laura
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Thank you for the quick heads-up and for the artifacts. We have triaged this as a P1 and engineering has identified a high-confidence mitigation. Immediate steps we're taking now:
- Rolling back the weekend "optimized-batching" change for your tenant and the affected model variant (will be visible within ~10–15 minutes).
- Applying a targeted ingress throttle for your integration to dampen retry storms (expected <5 minutes to go live).
- Increasing model/gateway timeouts temporarily while we validate the rollback.

Our engineering manager (Laura) has opened INF-4721 and is leading a hotfix to address the TTL/batching interaction root cause. We're treating this as top priority. I'll update you as soon as the rollback and throttling are active. Please hold off on replaying failed requests while we stabilize — replaying will only make the queue worse.

We aim to have the rollback + ingress throttle in place within 30 minutes and a full patch within 6 hours.

Subject: Postmortem/Status update: Acme production outage (5xx/504)

All —

Summary: On 2026-03-09 08:40 PST Acme reported elevated 5xx/504 and 429 errors affecting their realtime product. Root cause: regression introduced by the "optimized-batching" rollout (2026-03-08, commit f9c8b2) that exposed a KV-cache TTL alignment bug when batch sizes spiked, resulting in cache thrash, request queueing, and gateway/model timeouts. Retry storms exacerbated the congestion.

Actions taken:
- 2026-03-09 11:05 PST: Rollback of optimized-batching for affected variant (rolled back for Acme + global canary).
- 2026-03-09 11:10 PST: Targeted ingress throttling for Acme and temporary timeout increases.
- 2026-03-09 13:00 PST: Hotfix branch created (INF-4721). Canary applied; observed recovery of latency and error rates.

Customer impact: Acme's error rate peaked at ~18% for ~35 minutes; degraded UX for chat/search for end users. Customer SRE paused replays at our request which prevented further amplification.

Next steps / asks:
- Engineering to complete hotfix and full rollout (Laura) — ETA 6 hours from now for full validation.
- CS/Sales to coordinate a customer comms timeline and propose a goodwill credit (Marissa/Jonas) — suggested credit: 10% of March invoice (pending finance approval).
- Eng/Infra to add a rate-limiter guardrail and better observability for batching/KV churn metrics (owner: infra team).

I will brief the execs in the 4pm sync and attach a short postmortem once INF-4721 is closed. Please escalate any objections to the proposed credit to me directly.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Operations
